newsitem.title: UK: Refining margins in Jan "very disappointing" - BP.
newsitem.headline: Refining margins in Jan "very disappointing" - BP.

text.p: British Petroleum BP L said on Tuesday margins at its refineries in January were "very disappointing", adding some of its business managers were considering cutting crude throughput.
"Our refining margins in January were very disappointing," said Rolf Stomberg, chief executive of BP Oil.
"Decisions are being taken decentrally but its not surprising that some business managers are considering cuts," he told reporters after BP reported a 30 percent rise in next profit in 1996.

Some European oil refiners have already cut production and others are considering following suit because of poor returns on sales of refined products in a weakening late winter heating oil market, oil traders said.

Earlier, BP said refining margins in the last three months of 1996 recovered to $2.30 a barrel from $1.63 a barrel the previous quarter, thanks largely to lower product stock levels and an early cold snap in December which boosted heating oil demand.
At $2.20 a barrel for the whole of 1996, margins were 29 percent up on 1995, BP's finance director John Buchanan said.
